title: India Eye Series-Clinching Win as Run Feast Moves to Hyderabad for Fourth T20I
excerpt: Leading 2-1, India can close out the five-match series against the West Indies on Wednesday at a Hyderabad venue built for big scores.
body:
• India lead the five-match T20I series 2-1, and a win in the fourth match in Hyderabad on Wednesday seals the series 3-1; a West Indies win levels it at 2-2.
  • India's top order has dominated the series — Abhishek Sharma hit 69 off 30 balls in Indore as India posted 223 and won by 14 runs.
  • West Indies remain dangerous: Sherfane Rutherford (172 runs) is the series' top scorer and Shai Hope (159 runs) chased down 249 in Ranchi with a 45-ball century.
  • Hyderabad's Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium averaged about 209 for first innings across this year's IPL matches, pointing to another high-scoring game.

India's batters will look for another run feast when the fourth T20 International against the West Indies is played at the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium in Hyderabad on Wednesday, with the series on the line. India lead the five-match series 2-1 after their 14-run win in Indore, and one more victory closes out the rubber 3-1. The West Indies, who must win to level at 2-2 and force a decider, need to find a way to contain the most destructive top order in T20 cricket right now, according to PTI.

Top Order Doing the Damage

Sanju Samson, Abhishek Sharma and Ishan Kishan have come good in turns, and India have rarely needed their middle order. Captain Shreyas Iyer set the tone with a maiden T20I hundred in the series opener. Samson and Kishan then made the second game a contest India still lost, before Abhishek took over in Indore, smashing 69 off 30 balls with six fours and five sixes to set up a total of 223. The one concern for the hosts is the flip side of that dominance: Tilak Varma, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Naman Dhir have had little time in the middle, and they would need to be ready if the top three fail together while chasing a big target.

"I guess our plan B is to just be as defensive as possible and try to make him get singles and twos."

— Shamar Springer, West Indies all-rounder, on bowling to Abhishek Sharma

West Indies Keep Punching

The visitors have been outgunned, not outclassed. Sherfane Rutherford is the leading run-getter of the series with 172 runs at an average above 57 and a strike rate of 189, including 12 sixes in three games. Captain Shai Hope has 159 runs at a strike rate of 182, and his 45-ball 102 in Ranchi powered a chase of 249 in 18.3 overs — proof this batting line-up can hunt down almost anything. In Indore, Shimron Hetmyer (43), Kamil Pooran (42) and Springer (35 not out) dragged the chase close before Arshdeep Singh's three wickets sealed India's win; spinner Naman Dhir's two for 39 also gave India a useful extra option.

Hyderabad Promises Runs

The venue points to more of the same. The Hyderabad ground recorded an average first-innings score of around 209 across seven IPL matches this year, and it has staged successful T20I chases of 208 and 187, IANS reported. India's last T20I here, against Bangladesh in 2024, produced 297 for six — Samson made 111 off 47 balls in a 133-run win — and Samson, Abhishek and Nitish, all Sunrisers Hyderabad players, will be on home turf. Dew is not expected to be a major factor under lights, so the toss should matter less than in earlier games. For diaspora fans following the tour, Wednesday's match is the pivot of the series: an India win ends the contest, a West Indies win sets up a winner-takes-all finale.

India squad: Shreyas Iyer (captain), Ishan Kishan, Sanju Samson, Naman Dhir, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Tilak Varma, Abhishek Sharma, Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Arshdeep Singh, Kuldeep Yadav, Prince Yadav, Ravi Bishnoi, Mayank Yadav. West Indies squad: Shai Hope (captain), Jewel Andrew, Shimron Hetmyer, Amir Jangoo, Kamil Pooran, Rovman Powell, Sherfane Rutherford, Quentin Sampson, Roston Chase, Keemo Paul, Romario Shepherd, Shamar Springer, Matthew Forde, Akeal Hosein, Shamar Joseph, Gudakesh Motie.
